draft.title: Technology in operations
card: An automated production line uses machines to do repeated tasks with little human input. Robots can lift, weld or pack with the same result each time, so there are fewer errors and less waste.
Computer-aided design (CAD) is software used to draw and test a product on screen. Faults can be found and fixed before anything is made, which saves materials and time.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is software that learns from data to make decisions or spot patterns. A business can use it to detect faulty products or predict when a machine needs repair.
Online services let customers order, book or get help over the internet. This can cut staffing and premises costs, and it cuts the errors that come from taking orders by hand.
draft.remember: Technology can cut costs and errors, but each type suits a different job.

a.q: Zara's furniture business in Geelong tests a new chair design on screen and finds a weak leg before any timber is cut. Which technology is this?
a.why: Drawing and testing a product on screen before it is made is computer-aided design. An automated line or robots would be used when making the chair, not when testing the design on screen.
a.clue: Think about what happens before anything is made.

b.q: Tom runs a bakery in Ballarat. He wants to cut errors caused by staff writing down phone orders wrongly. Which change would best fix this problem?
opts: An online ordering service for customers
A robot arm to pack the loaves
Computer-aided design of new loaf shapes
An automated oven line for baking bread
b.why: Customers enter their own orders online, so the order is not copied down by hand and the errors from writing it wrongly are cut. A robot arm or an automated oven line works on making and packing, and CAD works on design, so none of them touches how orders are taken.
b.clue: Where in the process do the errors happen?

b.best: An online ordering service for customers
